original_test_intent: Validate the two motherboard PSU-associated temperature sensors represented by TEMP_MB_PSU1~2, with exact identity, physical association and approved limits consistently shown in complete IB/OOB SDR, Sensor List and BMC Web evidence.
original_method: The platform owner expands the range into two exact names, maps each motherboard sensing point to its PSU bay, connector and power path, distinguishes it from PSU-internal telemetry, and automation passively collects the approved records and context.
manual_activity: The platform/power owner defines both exact MB_PSU records, their board coordinates and relationship to PSU bays, connectors and internal telemetry, approves operating limits and validates Web evidence; upper-fan evidence is not reused.
required_inputs: Exact TEMP_MB_PSU1 and TEMP_MB_PSU2 sensor names and populated count
Motherboard revision and per-sensor coordinate, connector, rail/feed and associated PSU bay/serial map
Definition separating motherboard probe, PSU inlet/outlet and PSU-internal controller telemetry
SDR entity/name/description plus Sensor List and Web mapping
Units, scale, tolerance, sampling/freshness, unavailable semantics and condition-specific limits
Same-target IB/OOB identity plus BMC/SDR/PSU/platform spec revisions
Secret-safe collectors and independent power/thermal/BMC recovery
safety_requirements: Bind exact row 1885 and exclude the duplicate upper-fan workflow
Resolve two exact owner-approved names rather than querying a literal tilde range
Do not equate an MB-side probe with PSU-internal temperature without approved mapping
Capture PSU identity, feed, redundancy, load/current and health passively
Do not power-control or hot-plug PSUs, change fans/thresholds/BMC, or clear logs
Retain complete IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List plus Web; stop on mapping, redundancy, power or thermal anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Verify source/variant, duplicate isolation and exact two-name expansion
Verify same-target motherboard/PSU topology and health read-only
Collect complete IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List, both exact records and BMC Web
Compare identity, value, unit, state and freshness with passive PSU/feed/load/SEL context
Perform no upper-fan substitution, PSU service/control, write, log clear, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve motherboard measurement-point to PSU bay/connector/power-path map
Define relationship to PSU-internal inlet/outlet/controller telemetry
Provide condition-specific ranges and required redundancy/load state
Review both records and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a two-row map from exact sensor string to motherboard coordinate, connector/power path, PSU bay/serial and sensing source, then reconcile all management views under a recorded passive power state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Prevents a literal range token and ambiguous `MB_PSU` label from being accepted without proving two physical measurement points.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The same-code upper-fan Web case and PSU-internal sensors do not substitute for motherboard-side PSU thermal coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Misidentifying the sensing point can apply the wrong thermal limit or hide a connector/board hot spot; power-domain intervention is outside this review.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Row 1885 consistently targets a two-member motherboard PSU thermal family. Missing physical semantics are required project inputs; the same-code upper-fan row is a distinct source identity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The passive two-sensor comparison is identifiable after owner supplies exact names, physical mapping and limits under ED-35/36.

review_improvement: Separates the MB_PSU probes from both upper-fan and PSU-internal telemetry and makes PSU topology, load and redundancy context part of acceptance.
independent_technical_reasoning: A motherboard sensor labelled for a PSU can measure a connector, rail hot spot, airflow region or PSU-adjacent board location rather than the PSU controller's internal temperature. Exact physical and power-path mapping is therefore necessary before selecting limits or comparing views.
